title: Emergency admin access playbook and break-glass controls for RBAC v2
creator: Marisol Chen
description: Problem: As we migrate to RBAC v2 and tighten SSO/SAML mappings, on-call and SRE teams have fewer standing admin principals. We need a formal, auditable emergency admin procedure (break-glass) that provides just-in-time elevated access for urgent incidents while minimizing blast radius and preserving forensic evidence. This ticket defines the playbook, implementation constraints, logging requirements, and tests for an emergency admin flow that integrates with RBAC v2, SSO/SAML, audit logging, and our incident tooling.
problem_statement: Current informal 'root' walkthroughs (shared keys, ad-hoc SSH to control plane) are inconsistent and leave gaps in audit trails. Without a standardized break-glass mechanism, incident responders risk bypassing RBAC and SSO, causing compliance violations and making post-incident reviews harder.
proposed_solution: Implement a time-limited, JIT (just-in-time) break-glass workflow that issues ephemeral admin sessions tied to a generated emergency token. Requirements: 1) Witnessed two-person approval by 'on-call primary' + 'security approver' OR automated approval if incident is declared in pagerduty with active status and primary on-call unreachable for >15 minutes; 2) Session limited to scoped admin role mapped in RBAC v2 (not global root) with minimum necessary privileges; 3) Enforce SSO/SAML step-up authentication and MFA for the requesting user (or require an audit-only emergency service account that is still SSO-authenticated); 4) All actions recorded in immutable audit logs with generated correlation_id; 5) Automatic timer to expire session after max 4 hours or earlier on manual revoke; 6) Immediate alerting to PagerDuty and Slack #sec-ops channel when break-glass is granted and revoked.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc approved by Security and SRE
End-to-end demo of break-glass issuance and revocation with RBAC v2 role mapping
Audit logs include correlation_id, requester SAML nameid, approvers, TTL, scope, and list of distinct admin API calls made
Automated test that simulates pagerduty-triggered emergency approvals and verifies session expiry
No ability to bypass SSO/SAML when using break-glass; all sessions must be tied to a verifiable identity or emergency service principal
Alerting and on-call notification verified in staging and a drill run scheduled in production
implementation_notes: We will implement the flow inside the control plane service that issues tokens for console + API access. Leverage existing JIT token infra from ENG-5021 and the audit-log sink implemented in ENG-5090. Key items: - Token generation endpoint must require an approval proof signed by the approver's SAML session or a PagerDuty webhook signed secret. - Tokens are minted as short-lived OAuth2 bearer credentials with an 'emergency' flag and attached scope claim enumerating allowed admin actions. - RBAC v2 must enforce scope claims; any attempt to escalate beyond scope should be denied and audited. - UI in Console: a single hazardous action button "Request Emergency Admin" that shows required approvers and estimated TTL. - Break-glass requests and approvals must populate a structured audit record (RFC format) and be exported to our immutable S3 bucket and SIEM (Chronicle).
audit_log_schema_requirements: Each break-glass audit entry must be JSON lines with fields: correlation_id, request_id, requester_nameid, requester_email, requester_saml_issuer, approvers[], approver_methods[], approval_timestamps[], scope_claims[], token_id, token_ttl_seconds, issued_at, revoked_at|null, actions_performed:[timestamp, api_endpoint, parameters_redacted, result_code], service_account_used|null, incident_ticket_number|null. Logs must be write-once and retained for 7 years in compliance archive. Alerts sent to #sec-ops must include correlation_id and minimal context (no sensitive params).
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: A compromised break-glass flow could enable long-lived admin sessions. Mitigations: default TTL small (4h), require 2 approvers or PD webhook + secondary approver within 15m, require MFA step-up, break-glass tokens are unusable for non-console paths unless explicitly allowed. Additional mitigation: automatic post-session credential rotation for any secrets touched during the session and mandatory postmortem form completed by approver within 24h.
operational_playbook: 1) Incident owner opens incident and marks it as 'requires break-glass' with incident ID; 2) Requestor hits 'Request Emergency Admin' in Console; 3) System validates SSO session and prompts for MFA step-up; 4) Approval flow triggers PagerDuty notifications to security approver and primary; 5) After two approvals (or PD webhook condition), token minted with correlation_id and TTL; 6) Token usage streams to audit sink and real-time watch rules analyze for anomalous API patterns; 7) If an alarm fires or TTL expires, session auto-revoked and PD escalation runs; 8) On resolution, approver uploads incident notes and selects if any secrets require rotation.
testing_and_drills: - Staging drill: simulate on-call unreachable path by using PD webhook flow and validate auto-approval path. - Chaos test: simulate mid-session revoke and verify graceful rollback of in-flight admin tasks. - Compliance audit test: random sample of break-glass events must contain non-empty approver list and completed postmortem. - Load test: ensure audit sink and SIEM ingestion handle spikes when multiple teams perform break-glass concurrently.
